topics.topic: The closed typed model and fields representing live and erased Customers
questions: What closed runtime-model form represents the Customer before and after erasure?
Replace the prose-only erased mark and its instant with the complete typed Customer field or typed variant declarations that represent the live and erased forms.

What closed model facts represent the erased mark and its instant: does one timestamp both mark and date erasure, are a separate status or boolean and timestamp stored, or is erasure represented by a distinct tombstone model or variant?

Is the erased state represented by one nullable instant that is itself the mark, by a separate mark/status plus an instant, or by a distinct value model; and what identity, if any, does that value model have?
Replace this prose-only addition with an explicit declaration of every retained erasure field and its type, including whether the mark and its instant are one field or separate fields.

quotes: Field names, types, formal optionality and every answer shape belong to State 6; orders, replay mechanisms, correction semantics and token scopes belong to State 2 (State 0, "Carried to later states"; codex round-01 T5).
judgement.why: P1 already decides that complete typed model forms, fields and optionality are State 6 output rather than a SPEC_STANDARD §5 obligation of State 1, and the revision did not change that allocation.

precedent.topic: Complete typed field declarations and optionality for every State 1 model
quotes: Field names, types, formal optionality and every answer shape belong to State 6; orders, replay mechanisms, correction semantics and token scopes belong to State 2 (State 0, "Carried to later states"; codex round-01 T5).

SPEC_STANDARD §5's rule that every field is declared with its type is a rule of the specification's `models` section, and that section is State 6's output (`skills/spec-authoring/AUTHORING_SEQUENCE.md`): State 6 writes each model here with every fact as a typed field, and declares there what this state decides — its identity and its kind (§5, §15.1.1).
precedent.why: Complete field names, types and formal optionality are expressly assigned to State 6, so §5 governs that later models output rather than this State 1 domain-fact inventory.

topics.topic: Whether an erased Customer retains its created instant
questions: Does an erased Customer retain its created instant because every Customer carries it, or is that instant removed as one of every other fact but the identity?
Does an erased Customer lose its created instant, despite the unit saying that a Customer carries the instant it was created, or does that instant survive erasure?

judgement.why: The Customer's created instant is its written-once recorded instant, and the erased form expressly removes that instant while retaining only customer_ref, the erased mark and its instant.

topics.topic: Whether erasure advances and retains the Customer revision and last-changed instant
questions: Does an accepted customer erasure first advance the revision as required for every accepted change of a Customer's own facts, or is erasure an exception that removes the revision without advancing it?

Is erasure an exception that replaces the Customer with an identity-preserving tombstone having no revision or last-changed instant, or must the accepted change first advance and retain the revision and last-changed instant as the unit's unconditional revision rule requires?

quotes:
A Project and a Customer carry a revision, an ordinal starting at 1 that
  accepted change of its own facts moves by one.

A Customer's last-changed instant moves by: a correction of its contact,
  kind or fiscal data; restricting and lifting; ending and resuming the
  relationship. An erasure does not move it: it removes the revision and the
  last-changed instant with every other fact but the identity, and records
  the erased mark with its own instant (M04, A04 rule 1; owner, 2026-11-24).
judgement.why: A successful erasure is an accepted change of the Customer's own facts, so the first obligation requires its revision and paired last-changed instant to advance while the second forbids that advance and removes both.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
